markdown_report:
At 20% progress, retain **bounded curriculum weighting of the existing 16 negatives**, restoring diagnostic coverage before interpretation. This remains an experiment; no new performance is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) The prior multi-negative experiment scored 0.5900 versus the cold start’s 0.5425; these historical results do not isolate causality. (2) Zero inspected batches establish missing diagnostic coverage, not inadequate separation or absent production masks. (3) Users report broad associations displacing specific matches and insufficient identifiable relevance. Hardness weighting addresses both indirectly, without establishing ownership, compatibility or current intent.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [RotatE](https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/KnowledgeGraphEmbedding/blob/master/codes/model.py) establishes detached self-adversarial weighting; originality is limited. Its binary logistic objective differs from weighting inside candidate CE’s partition function. (2) [Decoupled Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06848) motivates separating aggregate gradient pressure from negative allocation: mean-one weights preserve their sum, not exponential mass. (3) [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) motivates false-negative caution. High scores do not establish dislike, and popularity effects remain dataset-dependent. (4) [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) and [TemProxRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) motivate separate text and temporal experiments; pretrained initialization and omitted sensitivity outcomes limit direct transfer.

The framework separates **competition** through loss weighting, **identification** through text, and **context** through temporal features. Measurement coverage and checkpoint consistency span all three directions. Within competition, distinguish gradient pressure, allocation and scheduling.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Benefits (+) and limitations (−) accompany every assessment.

| Atomic idea | Assessments |
|---|---|
| Bounded curriculum CE | O 2: +controlled adaptation, −established weighting; P 6: +cheap experiment, −false negatives; U 6: +specific discrimination hypothesis, −indirect relevance; M 5: +restores coverage, −no measured separation deficit; D 4: +local loss, −instrumentation |
| Joint title residual | O 4: +constrained adaptation, −known fusion; P 7: +identification, −sparse titles; U 8: +specific connections, −usefulness uncertain; M 4: +auditable features, −no diagnosed text deficit; D 6: +pooling, −predictor changes |
| Learned time-gap bias | O 3: +adaptation, −known modeling; P 6: +occasion sensitivity, −timestamp noise; U 7: +current-interest hypothesis, −no intent labels; M 3: +sensitivity measurement, −outcomes omitted; D 6: +few parameters, −timestamp interfaces |

For the selected idea, preserve K=16 candidates and detach weights. Warm up uniformly, then ramp α to 0.25. Weights sum to 16 and lie within [0.75,4.75], but increase negative exponential mass whenever scores differ. Consequently, this changes both aggregate pressure and allocation; it does not isolate hardness or prove curriculum benefits. Prioritize uniform versus ramped CE; a separately budgeted mass-preserving control can investigate allocation. Restore valid masked-target diagnostic batches to address the observed measurement failure. Track gradient concentration, score scale and training-positive collisions. Select solely by fixed macro validation HR@10; never combine predictions. Text and temporal alternatives remain follow-ups if weighting fails.

idea.description: Test bounded, gradually introduced, detached weighting of the same 16 uniformly sampled negatives inside the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Train exactly one independent model per category. Restore measured masked-target diagnostic coverage as instrumentation, without presenting it as an accuracy improvement. Describe the primary intervention as a joint change in negative-gradient allocation, aggregate gradient pressure and its schedule.
idea.motivation: The prior multi-negative experiment provides promising historical context, while current diagnostics provide no measured separation results. The intervention hypothesizes that emphasizing confusing alternatives can reduce two user-facing failures: broadly related items displacing stronger contextual matches, and recommendations with weak identifiable connections to history. Neither benefit is established, and interaction-only supervision cannot establish compatibility, ownership, redundancy, mood or current purpose. The observed model-facing failure addressed directly is zero inspected diagnostic batches; harmful embedding collapse, inadequate convergence and excessive recency dependence are not established. At 20% progress, this localized experiment remains more feasible than jointly introducing text or temporal architecture changes. RotatE substantially limits the novelty claim, and exponential-mass coupling limits mechanistic attribution.
idea.implementation_notes:
Modify the supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing unavailable source. First document its actual objective, negative count, eligibility, replacement policy, masking, terminal allocation, reductions, optimizer, schedule, clipping and checkpoint rules. The source is absent from this writing input, so these are integration specifications rather than a verified executable train.py replacement. If the actual starting configuration is not uniform candidate CE with K=16, identify the resulting combined intervention explicitly. Historical scores do not authorize reading other trials or reusing their checkpoints.

Predeclare the primary comparison as uniform K=16 candidate CE versus the same objective with ramped detached weights. Train complete four-category configurations only when the remaining shared budget permits. Retain the unchanged supplied baseline as historical benchmark context; any newly trained matched control must start independently. Preserve architecture, corruption, sampled windows, endpoint allocation, optimizer, clipping and checkpoint policy so weighting and its schedule constitute the declared treatment. Do not add text, temporal features, a mining model, a larger scoring pool or independently fitted auxiliary scores.

Use zero-based epoch e and alpha_e = 0.25 * clamp((e - 20) / 40, 0, 1). Thus alpha is zero through epoch 20 and reaches 0.25 at epoch 60. For each valid hidden target, let p be its positive logit and n_j its 16 negative logits. Compute r = softmax(beta * n.detach()), with fixed beta=1, and w_j = (1-alpha_e) + alpha_e*16*r_j. Explicitly detach the weights. Alpha controls interpolation; beta is inverse temperature. They are different parameters. Do not tune either after inspecting treatment results. The weights sum to 16 and lie within [1-alpha_e, 1+15*alpha_e], hence within [0.75,4.75] over the proposed schedule. Candidate multiplicities retain the audited sampling semantics.

Optimize L = logsumexp([p, n_1+log(w_1), ..., n_16+log(w_16)]) - p using a stable implementation and the baseline across-target/example reduction. State that reduction's exact denominator in the implementation record. At alpha=0 this is ordinary candidate CE. Compute detached softmax weights and the loss partition in float32 when mixed precision is used, while preserving the baseline optimizer procedure. Handle batches with no valid targets using the documented baseline policy rather than an empty reduction. This is a weighted candidate-ranking objective, not an unbiased full-catalog likelihood estimator.

Mean-one weights do not preserve negative exponential mass. Let M0=sum_j exp(n_j), Mw=sum_j w_j*exp(n_j), and Z=exp(p)+Mw. With detached weights, dL/dp=exp(p)/Z-1 and dL/dn_j=w_j*exp(n_j)/Z. Because softmax(n_j) and exp(n_j) are positively ordered, Mw>=M0, with strict inequality for alpha>0 and unequal finite negative scores. Thus the method both increases positive attraction through Mw/Z and redistributes negative gradients. It does not isolate better relative discrimination. Standard CE already emphasizes higher-scoring negatives; the proposed method adds emphasis. Although weight ratios are bounded, negative-gradient concentration is not equivalently bounded because exp(n_j) also contributes. Weighting is invariant to a common logit shift, but sensitive to score scale, which evolves during training. Do not describe alpha as RotatE's temperature or claim RotatE's binary logistic objective is algebraically equivalent to this partition-weighted CE.

If budget remains after the primary complete comparison, the first optional mechanistic control is mass-preserving weighting. Compute log_c = stop_gradient(logsumexp(n)-logsumexp(n+log(w))) for each target, using detached logits consistently; use negative offsets log(w)+log_c. The forward negative mass then equals M0 at the current logits, while detached normalization preserves a redistributed surrogate gradient. Its forward scalar equals ordinary CE at the current logits, so document explicitly that its backward update differs through stop-gradient; this is an update-rule control rather than a distinct ordinary differentiable scalar objective. Differentiating through the normalization would cancel the intended reallocation. The rescaled weights no longer retain the original mean-one sum or [0.75,4.75] bounds. An additional pressure-only control, if separately affordable, assigns every negative the detached multiplier Mw/M0; this matches the full method's aggregate pressure at identical logits while retaining ordinary CE's within-negative allocation. Independently trained trajectories will diverge, so pressure is not matched across complete runs. Constant, reversed or differentiable-weight schedules and learned score scales remain deferred alternatives. The primary uniform-versus-ramp comparison cannot attribute gains specifically to a curriculum; that requires a constant-weight control and additional budget.

Use the same purpose-separated seed-42 RNG design in matched configurations if sample matching is implemented. Keep user/window and corruption streams independent of K or weighting. Distinguish any RNG-stream change from the untouched host baseline. Record sampled-window, target and corruption hashes when claiming matched examples; a shared global seed alone does not establish matching. Optional control configurations receive identical initialization procedures, candidates and prescribed training opportunities, but their actual GPU time must still be recorded. Avoid claiming matched compute solely because there are no extra model forward passes.

Preserve the audited negative proposal, replacement policy and history exclusions in both primary configurations. Always exclude the current positive, PAD and MASK. Audit collisions with known training positives, including other hidden targets, without silently changing eligibility in one arm. Do not add deduplication or broader history exclusions only to the treatment. If a common eligibility correction is required, document it as another change relative to the supplied baseline. Use only training information for exclusions. Repeated candidates retain multiplicity when sampling with replacement; report unique counts and duplicates. Preserve documented handling of empty or small eligible sets. Unobserved items are uncertain negatives, and high model scores do not establish actual dislike.

Restore DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) coverage with an independent disposable loader from the family-specific sampler. Diagnostic tuples remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), all B x L, preserving the original one-negative semantics; the K=16 training tensor stays internal to the training loss. Inspect up to 20 batches or loader exhaustion, recording inspected batches, valid reserved-mask target counts, invalid positions and explicit reasons for unavailable quantities. Do not consume the active production iterator or alter production RNG state. Retain diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), metrics and metric_definitions. Zero coverage must remain an unavailable measurement requiring investigation, not a passing result or proof that production lacks masked targets. Training margins are descriptive and cannot establish held-out separation.

Record measured positive-minus-negative margins and negative-beats-positive rates under the fixed diagnostic protocol. Raw margin magnitude is score-scale sensitive; fixed-candidate ordering is invariant to a common positive rescaling. On at most four explicitly captured production batches per category, summarize detached log(Mw)-p, sigmoid(log(Mw)-p), negative-gradient allocation softmax(n+log(w)), its entropy and effective sample size 1/sum_j allocation_j^2, plus uniform-reference allocation softmax(n). Distinguish sampling weights w/16 from actual negative-gradient allocation. Record score dispersion and item/feature norms to expose scale changes. Bounded consumed-record captures can support same-forward pipeline and loss auditing, but absence remains unavailable, captures need not correspond to the selected checkpoint, and they do not certify all training steps or gradients. Preserve the actual scalar-reduction formula in audit records.

For optional history-only risk diagnostics, use training-frequency deciles to summarize assigned negative-weight and gradient mass, score–log-frequency correlation and known-training-positive collision mass relative to uniform. Retrospective prefix probes may measure overlap with later observed events within training histories, but must remain diagnostic, must not use validation/test labels, and must never feed those later events into prefix inputs. Such overlap and co-occurrence are suspicion proxies, not true false-negative labels or evidence of dislike. If genuinely run on the twenty designated training users, report recommendation head share, catalog coverage, exposure Gini and recommendation popularity relative to historical popularity. State the small sample and whether statistics aggregate across users; do not infer simulator diversity/conformity traits. Aggregate HR@10 alone cannot establish popularity balance. These optional diagnostics consume budget and must not displace the primary complete comparison.

Keep view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. No architecture changes are required by the selected loss. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and observed timestamps. Unavailable review text, ratings, item categories/prices/stores and simulator traits are excluded. Embedding angular alignment scores do not establish harmful collapse, diversity or representation quality. Omitted sensitivity outcomes do not establish a preferred recency direction.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], supplied splits, Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Respect the SASREC_EPOCHS=200 environment default. Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Training, diagnostics, debugging, failed trials and comparison configurations consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; four concurrent slots do not reduce summed GPU cost. Predeclare optional controls and diagnostic limits before observing outcomes, and launch them only with sufficient remaining budget.

Keep the bidirectional BERT4Rec backbone with reserved-mask training and appended-mask inference. Supervised target occurrences remain hidden; never introduce visible shifted targets. Preserve baseline corruption, including any permitted legitimate earlier repeated items. At inference retain the final L-1 observed events, append MASK without target information, left-pad and read the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Require baseline-supported sequence capacity. Each category loads exactly one selected independently trained model/checkpoint. Preserve the embedded predictor writer, architecture configuration, reserved IDs, mappings and all four routes. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendation candidates. No ensembles, independently fitted expert mixtures, checkpoint averaging, rank voting or auxiliary fitted scores are permitted. Do not claim checkpoint/predictor parity without fresh-process verification using identical histories and candidate IDs; live identity checks do not establish deployment parity.

Select solely by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10: 200 validation users/category, one positive and 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Preserve host users, candidates, validation schedule, stopping, checkpoint selection and tie rules. Report supplied per-category and macro results without fabricating uncertainty or full-catalog improvements. If paired user outcomes are unavailable, paired uncertainty is unavailable. Any available user bootstrap conditions on fitted models and candidates and excludes training-seed and adaptive-selection uncertainty. Freeze final selection before the host's untouched held-out evaluation. The twenty-user simulator provides qualitative evidence only if actually executed and cannot replace the selection metric.

Main risks are reinforcing uncertain false negatives, amplifying score-scale effects, memorizing repeated targets, learning popularity shortcuts and adaptively selecting favorable validation noise. Bounded weights limit the added multiplier but do not eliminate these risks. Preserve baseline regularization and stopping, report all inspected configurations/checkpoints and GPU costs, and avoid post-hoc schedule tuning. Keep the title-residual alternative as the strongest distinct follow-up for identifiable relevance: any future scratch-trained text branch must be jointly trained inside the same BERT4Rec and mask target text with target identity. Temporal biases remain separate and must use only observed timestamps, with unknown time for the appended mask. Neither alternative is warranted as an established remedy by the supplied diagnostics.
idea.pseudocode:
Audit supplied corrected BERT4Rec and record actual loss, K, sampler,
replacement, exclusions, reductions, corruption and checkpoint rules.
Declare uniform-K=16 versus ramped-weight-K=16 comparison and budget.
Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42.
Keep comparison models independent and never reuse another trial's checkpoint.

For each declared configuration:
    For category in the fixed four-category order:
        Initialize one supplied corrected BERT4Rec with seed 42.
        Use the same declared RNG-stream scheme across matched configurations.
        For epoch e in range(at_most_200):
            alpha = 0 for uniform control
            Otherwise alpha = 0.25 * clamp((e - 20) / 40, 0, 1)
            For exactly 200 batches:
                Sample baseline windows and unchanged reserved-mask corruption.
                Encode sequence using model.log2feats(sequence).
                Gather features only at valid supervised masked positions.
                Sample K=16 negatives under the shared audited policy.
                Compute positive logits p and negative logits n using predict_score.
                Cast loss-side logits to float32 if mixed precision is used.
                r = softmax(n.detach(), dim=-1)  # beta=1
                w = ((1-alpha) + alpha*16*r).detach()
                negative_offsets = log(w)
                If separately declared mass-preserving control:
                    log_c = (logsumexp(n.detach())
                             - logsumexp(n.detach()+log(w))).detach()
                    negative_offsets += log_c
                If separately declared pressure-only control:
                    log_c = (logsumexp(n.detach()+log(w))
                             - logsumexp(n.detach())).detach()
                    negative_offsets = broadcast(log_c)
                per_target_loss = logsumexp(concat(p, n+negative_offsets)) - p
                Apply documented baseline across-target/example reduction.
                Apply unchanged backward, clipping, optimizer and schedule order.
                Capture only the predeclared bounded audit records.
            Apply unchanged host-compatible checkpoint-selection procedure.
        Save exactly one selected checkpoint with matching configuration/mappings.
        Run independent disposable diagnostic loader for up to 20 batches.
        Record inspected batches, valid masks, margins and unavailable reasons.
        Return measured metrics and metric_definitions through preserved APIs.

For bounded captured batches:
    Compute baseline and weighted negative log-mass using logsumexp.
    Report aggregate pressure, gradient allocation entropy/ESS and score scale.
    Audit observed-training-positive collisions without modifying one arm's sampler.
    Mark unsupported provenance and deployment checks unavailable.

Emit matching working/predict.py with all four category routes.
At inference:
    Load exactly one selected checkpoint for the requested category.
    sequence = left_pad(last_L_minus_1(history) + [MASK], L)
    position = greatest index with sequence[position] != PAD
    Score real candidates from model.log2feats(sequence)[position].
Verify emitted-predictor/checkpoint scores in a fresh process when executed.
Obtain category and macro validation HR@10 only from the pinned host evaluator.
Record all configurations, checkpoint evaluations, failures and summed GPU-seconds.
Freeze one final configuration before untouched held-out evaluation.
Never combine checkpoints or independently trained predictions.

originality.positive: A precisely specified adaptation places detached, uniformly interpolated self-adversarial weights inside masked-item candidate CE and exposes pressure-versus-allocation controls.
originality.negative: RotatE establishes detached score-dependent weighting, and candidate CE already emphasizes high-scoring negatives. The proposed combination and schedule do not establish algorithmic novelty.

future_potential.positive: The localized intervention needs no additional mining forward passes and can yield useful evidence about negative-gradient allocation within a single BERT4Rec.
future_potential.negative: No measured separation deficit currently supports the mechanism. False negatives, score-scale dependence and sampled-validation selection may limit improvements in actual usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary loss requires a few stable tensor operations and leaves architecture and inference unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible comparisons require sampler auditing, explicit stop-gradient semantics, restored diagnostic coverage, bounded capture transport, runtime accounting and fresh-process predictor verification; optional controls add further integration and training cost.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the bidirectional masked-item backbone and rationale for hiding supervised targets.
limitations: Does not establish benefits from bounded negative weighting under the pinned Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: RotatE official implementation
contributions: Implements detached self-adversarial negative weights using softmax of inverse-temperature-scaled scores.
Establishes direct prior art for adapting negative emphasis using the current model.
limitations: Uses a knowledge-graph binary logistic objective with separately anchored positive and negative penalties, unlike candidate CE's shared partition function.
Does not establish recommendation gains or novelty for the proposed interpolation.

related_work.title: RotatE released configurations
contributions: Provides concrete released settings, including adversarial inverse temperatures of 1.0 or 0.5.
limitations: Those settings are not validated hyperparameters for this BERT4Rec task.

related_work.title: Decoupled Contrastive Learning
contributions: Analyzes coupling in contrastive objectives and motivates distinguishing aggregate pressure from allocation among negatives.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed mass-preserving stop-gradient control or establish a recommendation improvement.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning with Hard Negative Samples
contributions: Studies controllable negative hardness and provides context for evaluating hard-negative mechanisms.
limitations: Its setting and assumptions do not establish that high-scoring unobserved Amazon items are valid negatives.

related_work.title: Understanding the Behaviour of Contrastive Loss
contributions: Analyzes temperature-dependent hardness penalties, motivating explicit treatment of inverse temperature and score scale.
limitations: Does not isolate gains for the proposed BERT4Rec weighting schedule.

related_work.title: UFNRec
contributions: Documents false-negative concerns in sequential recommendation and investigates handling suspected false negatives.
limitations: Does not identify the true false-negative rate in this benchmark or validate the proposed weighting rule.

related_work.title: AHNS
contributions: Studies adaptive hard-negative sampling in collaborative filtering and motivates caution about suppressing relevant unobserved items.
limitations: Its collaborative-filtering evidence does not directly establish behavior in masked-item BERT4Rec.

related_work.title: Sequential-recommendation negative-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: The supplied summary compares sampling strategies across repeated experiments and reports accuracy/exposure trade-offs.
Motivates measuring popularity effects rather than assuming hardness necessarily worsens them.
limitations: Does not establish a matched-K, matched-compute BERT4Rec improvement for the proposed weighting rule.
Reported dataset-specific popularity effects cannot be assumed for the four required categories.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Supports investigating jointly learned text-based sequential representations as a separate identification direction.
limitations: Uses pretrained Longformer initialization, which is unsuitable for direct adoption under this task's restrictions.
Does not establish effectiveness of a small text encoder trained from scratch.

related_work.title: TemProxRec
contributions: Distinguishes absolute and relative temporal information in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Combines temporal modeling with other mechanisms and does not isolate an expected gain for this benchmark.
The supplied sensitivity outcomes do not justify imposing recency decay.
